item.content:encoded:
THE McDonald’s Fiji Fijian Drua Women utility back Josivini Naihamu emerged as the biggest winner of the night, claiming both the Encore Players’ Player of the Year and the prestigious McDonald’s Fiji Player of the Year awards during the annual awards at the Sofitel Resort and Spa last night.

Voted by her teammates for the Players’ Player accolade, Naihamu was also selected by head coach Mike Legge as the club’s outstanding performer of the season.

Naihamu enjoyed a superb campaign this season, scoring five tries in six appearances while consistently leading by example through her work ethic, commitment and influence within the squad.

item.title: ‘Lions’on glory hunt | Grammar shifts focus to national knockout
item.description: SUVA Grammar School (SGS) has quickly shifted its attention to the Vodafone Deans Under-18 national elimination rounds after successfully defending its Southern Zone Secondary Schools Rugby Union title. The defending champion edged Nasinu Secondary School 29-22 in Saturday’s final to retain their regional crown, giving the side valuable momentum heading into the next stage of the competition.
item.content:encoded:
SUVA Grammar School (SGS) has quickly shifted its attention to the Vodafone Deans Under-18 national elimination rounds after successfully defending its Southern Zone Secondary Schools Rugby Union title.

The defending champion edged Nasinu Secondary School 29-22 in Saturday’s final to retain their regional crown, giving the side valuable momentum heading into the next stage of the competition.

Team manager Evia Turaganivalu said the players were emotional after the victory and credited their success to faith and the commitment shown throughout the season.

“The team is a bit emotional now and we give back all the glory to God,” she said.

“He has been the main strength that has been pushing this team forward and for today we would like to thank Him and give back the glory and honour to Him for His blessings upon this team.”

Despite the achievement, Turaganivalu said the team would remain focused as they prepare for the national challenge.

“We’ll just take each day as it comes and continue with our preparation.”

SGS will now face Northern Zone fourth-placed side Ratu Luke Secondary School at midday on Saturday at either at Buckhurst Grounds or Suva Grammar grounds in the Vodafone Deans U18 national elimination round. In other U18 national elimination fixtures, Eastern Zone champions Lelean Memorial School will face Marist Brothers High School at midday at Saint Vincent College ground in Natovi, while Ratu Kadavulevu School will take on Ratu Sukuna Memorial School at 1.30pm. The Western Zone eliminations at Lawaqa Park in Sigatoka will see Ba Provincial Freebird Institute face Queen Victoria School at 10am, followed by Cuvu College against St John’s College at 1pm.

In the Southern Zone, Nasinu Secondary School will meet Holy Cross College at midday, while the North Zone eliminations at Ganilau Park in Savusavu will see Shri Guru Nanak Khalsa College face Ratu Navula College before Navatu Secondary School takes on Ra High School.

With the regional stage complete, SGS will now focus on building towards the national quarter-finals as they continue their pursuit of another Vodafone Deans U18 title.

item.title: Rokobuli sets sights on top finish
item.description: THE Nadi Police Rugby Club have achieved its first major target of the season by securing promotion to the Super Premier competition. The side has claimed the DEII Challenge Trophy and intends to defend it for the remainder of the season.
item.content:encoded:
THE Nadi Police Rugby Club have achieved its first major target of the season by securing promotion to the Super Premier competition.

The side has claimed the DEII Challenge Trophy and intends to defend it for the remainder of the season.

Team manager Jason Rokobuli says the side is determined to finish the job by claiming top spot in the TISA Insurance Nadi Rugby Union Competition.

Police sit second on the standings with 63 points after 16 rounds last weekend, trailing leaders Nawaka Rugby on 72 points.

Both teams, along with Korotabu Rugby at 3rd place with 60 points have secured its promotion to the Super Premier grade next season.

Rokobuli said the club entered the season with clear objectives and was pleased to have already achieved one of them.

“Our target at the start of the season was to finish in the top four, and we have managed to do that,” he said.

“We are the owners of the DEII Challenge Trophy now and we are keeping it this year. The next target is to try and top the Premier table so we can challenge for the TISA Insurance Trophy in the Super Premier category, which is currently held by Naduruniu Rugby Club.”

Despite several key players being unavailable due to higher representative duties, Rokobuli remains confident in the squad’s depth.

He said many of the club’s top players are involved with the McDonald’s Nadi Rugby team and the Western Police side, leaving the remaining squad members with an opportunity to step up.

“We are relying on the boys we have now to do the job for us this week and in the next game,” he said.

Rokobuli urged his players to remain committed to the goals established before the season began.

“I just want the boys to stay focused on the targets we set before the season. We know they can do the job for us.”

Rokobuli called on the public to continue supporting the Fiji Police Force in its fight against crime, saying rugby provides young people with opportunities to build better futures.

“Through rugby, youths are getting opportunities to secure jobs overseas, earn a living and create a better future for themselves. That is one positive way we can help steer them away from drugs and crime,” he said.

From the TISA Insurance Nadi Rugby Union Super Premier category, Naduruniu Rugby along with Mosi Rugby, Korobebe Rugby and Nabila Rugby have been demoted to the Premier category next season.

item.title: Ba football condemns online abuse
item.description: THE Ba Football Association has strongly condemned the alleged use of abusive and offensive language directed at its president, Praneel Dayal, on social media following Ba FC’s 4-1 victory over Lautoka FC on Sunday. The association said the incident involved alleged abusive and vulgar comments posted on TikTok by a market vendor.
item.content:encoded:
THE Ba Football Association has strongly condemned the alleged use of abusive and offensive language directed at its president, Praneel Dayal, on social media following Ba FC’s 4-1 victory over Lautoka FC on Sunday.

The association said the incident involved alleged abusive and vulgar comments posted on TikTok by a market vendor.

While acknowledging the passion and rivalry that comes with football, the Ba FA said there was a clear line between spirited support and personal abuse.

“Football is built on passion and rivalry, but there is a clear line between spirited support and personal abuse,” the association said in a statement.

The association said supporters have the right to express their views, but stressed that abusive, threatening or offensive conduct had no place in football or the wider community.

The matter has been referred to the relevant authorities for assessment.

“As the matter is now being dealt with through the appropriate channels, we will not make any further comment on the details at this time,” the association said.

Ba FA has also called on football supporters to uphold the values of respect, sportsmanship and fair play, particularly during intense rivalries.

The association said rivalries should remain on the football field and urged supporters to contribute towards creating a positive and safe environment for players, officials, administrators and fans.

The Ba FA said it remains committed to promoting football in a manner that reflects dignity, unity and mutual respect.

item.title: Rewa FC carries Fiji’s hopes
item.description: REWA FC will carry Fiji’s hopes on the continental stage when they compete in the 2026 OFC Men’s Champions League, and are ready to face some of Oceania’s top clubs. The tournament will be hosted in Fiji from August 9 to 22, with matches to be played in Churchill Park, Lautoka and 4R Stadium (Govind Park) Ba, giving Rewa the opportunity to compete in front of home supporters.
item.content:encoded:
REWA FC will carry Fiji’s hopes on the continental stage when they compete in the 2026 OFC Men’s Champions League, and are ready to face some of Oceania’s top clubs.

The tournament will be hosted in Fiji from August 9 to 22, with matches to be played in Churchill Park, Lautoka and 4R Stadium (Govind Park) Ba, giving Rewa the opportunity to compete in front of home supporters.

Rewa has been drawn in Group B alongside Lae City FC of Papua New Guinea, Galaxy FC of Vanuatu and qualifying tournament winners Tupapa Maraerenga FC of the Cook Islands.

The Delta Tigers reached the semi-finals of the competition in 2024 and will be looking to build on that performance when they return to the continental stage.

Tupapa Maraerenga secured their place in the tournament after winning the qualifying competition in Samoa earlier this year, marking their second consecutive qualification for the OFC Men’s Champions League.

Meanwhile, Galaxy FC and Lae City FC will make long-awaited returns to the competition as they look to challenge the region’s leading clubs.

The OFC Men’s Champions League will provide a tougher test for Rewa, with clubs bringing experienced players and squads that regularly compete at international level.

The tournament will mark the 25th edition of the competition since its inception in 1987 and remains the premier club football tournament in Oceania.

For Rewa, the competition is another opportunity to showcase Fiji football on the regional stage while giving local players valuable exposure against some of the best clubs in the Pacific. Playing as the host club, the Delta Tigers will look to use home advantage as they aim to progress through the group stage and make another strong run in the tournament. Rewa will open its campaign against Galaxy FC of Vanuatu on August 9 at Churchill Park in Lautoka, before facing Tupapa Maraerenga FC and Lae City FC in their remaining Group B matches.

item.title: Ba works on errors ahead of Skipper Cup opener against Suva
item.description: VINOD Patel Ba Rugby is stepping up preparations for a tough opening-round clash against Suva in the Skipper Cup Competition on Saturday at HFC Bank Stadium in Suva. Ba Rugby secretary Gabby Kautoga said preparations are progressing well, with the coaching staff working hard to address areas that let the side down in their previous encounter against Suva.
item.content:encoded:
VINOD Patel Ba Rugby is stepping up preparations for a tough opening-round clash against Suva in the Skipper Cup Competition on Saturday at HFC Bank Stadium in Suva.

Ba Rugby secretary Gabby Kautoga said preparations are progressing well, with the coaching staff working hard to address areas that let the side down in their previous encounter against Suva.

“Preparation for the Suva game is going on well and our coaching staff are working very hard. This is our fourth time playing Suva and we are working on our set pieces and errors from our last game against Suva last year,” Kautoga said.

Kautoga knows the challenge that awaits, but believes Ba can give the hosts a strong contest.

“We will give Suva a good game. We know that Suva is a big team and we are working on our discipline, which is so critical this season.”

The match will also provide an opportunity for several young Ba players to make their Skipper Cup debuts after impressing during the club competition.

“The boys are excited as a few boys will have their debut in the Skipper Cup this year. We have picked these boys from our club games and we believe in them to play and execute well on such a platform,” Kautoga added.

Kautoga has also called on Ba supporters to turn out in numbers and rally behind the team.

“We are requesting all our fans to come in numbers and cheer for our women, junior and senior teams in Suva.”

Ba will be looking to make a strong start to its Skipper Cup campaign when it takes on Suva on Saturday.

item.title: Golfers ready for ‘Classic’ tournament
item.description: THE Fiji Golf Classic 2026 will tee off this Friday at the Denarau Golf & Racquet Club, following tonight’s opening cocktail and tournament briefing. The three-day tournament runs from July 30 to August 1, bringing together golfers for a competitive battle on the Denarau course.
item.content:encoded:
THE Fiji Golf Classic 2026 will tee off this Friday at the Denarau Golf & Racquet Club, following tonight’s opening cocktail and tournament briefing.

The three-day tournament runs from July 30 to August 1, bringing together golfers for a competitive battle on the Denarau course.

Tonight’s opening cocktail party will give players and organisers an opportunity to come together ahead of the tournament, with the program including a tournament briefing, drinks and canapés.

The tournament will be played over three rounds, with the winner decided on the lowest aggregate score after the three rounds.

In the event of a tie, the winner will be decided through a three-hole playoff over the 18th, 10th and 18th holes.

The Fiji Golf Classic is expected to provide an exciting weekend of competition as golfers battle for top honours at Denarau.

The tournament will also be played under the Rules of Golf, together with the Fiji Golf Classic’s local rules and conditions, covering areas such as out of bounds, penalty areas and abnormal course conditions.

Tonight’s cocktail launch will include the tournament briefing, drinks and canapés as players prepare for what promises to be an exciting weekend of golf at Denarau.

item.title: Levuka to host school netters
item.description: THE Eastern Zone Secondary Schools Netball Competition will bring together the top school teams from across the region this Thursday and Friday at Nasau Park in Levuka. The two-day competition, scheduled for July 30 and 31, will feature the top four schools that reached the semi-finals from the Nasarawaqa, Tailevu and Levuka secondary school zones.
item.content:encoded:
THE Eastern Zone Secondary Schools Netball Competition will bring together the top school teams from across the region this Thursday and Friday at Nasau Park in Levuka.

The two-day competition, scheduled for July 30 and 31, will feature the top four schools that reached the semi-finals from the Nasarawaqa, Tailevu and Levuka secondary school zones.

Fiji Secondary Schools Netball Association vice-president Josua Qalo said the competition would feature teams competing in the Under-14, Under-15, Under-17, Under-19, open and boys’ categories.

“The Eastern Zone competition only comprises of the top four schools that have reached the semi-finals from the different zones,” Qalo said.

The tournament will provide schools with an opportunity to compete against some of the strongest netball programs in the Eastern Zone, while allowing officials to identify emerging talent for future representative pathways.

Qalo said hosting the competition in Levuka is also an important step towards reviving grassroots netball in the district.

“It’s an opportune time for schools back in Levuka, particularly allowing Levuka schools to take netball back to them,” he said.

The competition will feature established schools including Adi Cakobau School, while defending champions and other contenders will look to challenge for honours across the different grades.

The Eastern Zone Secondary Schools Netball Competition will conclude with the finals scheduled for the afternoon of the second day at Nasau Park in Levuka.
